newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth sets $20 mln ad campaign.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth sets $20 mln ad campaign.

text.p: BellSouth Corp on Thursday announced a new $20 million television ad campaign aimed at local phone service competition from AT&T Corp and other companies.

New ads were scheduled to begin airing on Monday, with the slogan "Nobody Knows a Neighbor Like a Neighbor," in hopes of reinforcing the regional Bell holding company's 100-year history as the local phone service provider for communities in its nine-state Southeast service region.
BellSouth's region stretches from Louisiana to Kentucky, North Carolina and Florida, and encompasses about 22 million customers.

Produced by the agency Merkley Newman Harty, the campaign changes course from existing BellSouth commercials that have emphasized products over service and featured celebrity spokespersons Dennis Miller, Courtney Cox and Dixie Carter.
BellSouth released two commercials on Thursday.
A 90-second spot focuses on the star of the new campaign -- a soft-spoken fictional BellSouth employee who lives in an equally fictional and idealized southern town.
Another 30-second ad promotes a Saturday service for businesses. Future ads were expected to address BellSouth's response to natural disasters and to emphasize other services for business.

"Change is the order of the day for a dynamic and expanding telecom industry...and we're determined to be better than any other company at serving our customers," said Jere Drummond, chief executive of the operating subsidiary, BellSouth Telecommunications Inc.
BellSouth said 228 companies have announced plans to offer service in its nine-state area and that 100 companies have already begun operating.
